title: On-call context resumer and sliding telemetry window collector
author: Elliot Ramirez
release_notes: Adds on-call context resumption and a sliding telemetry window collector to improve first-response speed and diagnosis. Backwards-compatible; feature gated behind experimental flag.
description:
Context and motivation: First responders frequently lose ephemeral UI context (open traces, selected log ranges, pinned screenshots) when a browser reloads or when they switch devices during an alert. That transient loss costs time and forces redundant searches. This PR introduces two coordinated pieces: a context resumer that persists minimal on-call state in an encrypted short-lived store, and a sliding telemetry window collector that lets responders attach a bounded recent telemetry slice to an incident for instant replay.

What this PR does (single-string narrative): - Adds a context-resumer service (incident-bot/context-resumer) that snapshots selected UI state (selected span id, time range, pinned logs, active runbook step) into an ephemeral store (encrypted, per-incident, TTL=20m). The store is implemented as a lightweight redis-backed shard with HMAC-signed tokens; by default the feature is gated off and enabled via the INCIDENT_RESUMER flag. - Implements a sliding-telemetry-window collector (observability/telemetry-window) which can capture a time-bounded set of traces, logs, and metrics samples around the time an on-call session is initiated. The window is configurable (default 2m pre-alert, 1m post-attach) and stored as an indexed tarball for quick download. - Wire-up in the UI: resume prompt on reconnect, 'attach recent telemetry' button in the incident sidebar, and a small status indicator showing retention TTL. - Security and privacy: snapshots exclude user inputs and secrets by default; there is a sanitize pipeline for logs that strips IPs and kube IDs. Admins can configure retention and disable storage. - Operational: adds metrics (resumer.hits, resumer.misses, telemetry.window.size_samples) and dashboard panels for hit-rate and storage churn.

Checklist: - [x] Design doc reviewed (ENG-9102) - [x] Unit tests for resumer serializer and TTL enforcement - [x] Integration test for restore flow (happy path + expired token) - [x] End-to-end UI smoke tests (resume flow + attach window) - [x] Security review: sanitize pipeline + threat model notes added - [x] Feature gated behind flag for gradual rollout

Commits summary: - 8f3b2cc: start(context-resumer): service scaffold + redis-backed ephemeral store - c4d2b7a: feat(telemetry-window): collector + archive writer and index - 9d1f5e4: ui(resume): add resume prompt and attach telemetry action - 3b6a2f1: test: integration tests for restore and telemetry attach - a7e9c33: ci: add e2e smoke stage and new metric assertions

Files touched (high-level): - incident-bot/pkg/resumer/* (service, handlers, serializer) - observability/telemetry/window_collector.go (collector + archiver) - webapp/src/components/ResumePrompt.tsx (resume UI) - scripts/e2e/resume_flow.spec.ts (e2e) - infra/redis/values.yaml (optional chart knobs) - docs/oncall/context-resumer.md (how-to and admin settings) - dashboards/resumer_panel.json (grafana panel)

Review conversation (highlights as single string): "Maya Chen (reviewer): Can we avoid storing full stack traces in the snapshot? We should only include trace IDs and a sampling of spans.
Elliot (author): Good catch — implemented a sanitize pass to store only IDs and up to 3 span summaries per trace. Added test to prove sensitive fields are dropped.
Ravi Singh (reviewer): The redis shard may grow if users trigger many snapshots quickly. What's the eviction plan?
Elliot: TTLs are enforced at write and we added a periodic GC job; also added a metric for eviction rate and a dashboard alert if total ephemeral keys exceed threshold.
Ana Torres (security): Ensure we have explicit opt-out for EU customers due to retention rules.
Elliot: Added a per-organization flag and documented the compliance controls in docs/oncall/context-resumer.md.

CI and merge notes: - Initial CI run failed intermittently on e2e (flaky start-up), tests rerun after increasing test timeouts. - All checks passed on second run (unit, lint, e2e-smoke). - Merge method: squash and merge. Release will enable feature in staged tenants via feature flag; ops will monitor resumer.hits and telemetry.window.size_samples during rollout.

Backward compatibility and migration: This is fully backward-compatible when feature flag is off. The telemetry archive format includes a version header and supports a migration path for future index changes.

Operational runbook excerpt (single-line friendly): If resumer.hits is low but resumer.errors is high, check redis auth and eviction logs; if telemetry.window.count spikes, temporarily tighten default duration or enable sampling.

Why this is unique / impact: Restoring UI context reduces time-to-first-action for responders by removing repetitive filtering and trace hunting. Combined with an attachable, bounded telemetry window, this feature turns the first responder session into an immediately actionable view of recent system state, lowering MTTR for transient incidents.

Follow-ups / TODOs: - Add per-incident manual deletion API for compliance - Add automatic anonymization plugins for additional PII types - Consider an on-disk fallback when redis quota is reached (feature gated)

Merge result: merged via squash (maintainer: Maya Chen)."
